ruling: - **R37. No fixed word cap, and no "STE" name.** Owner 12:54 CST Nov 11: "i thought i eliminated all STE requirements from everywhere in the repo weeks ago (along with hard limits like 30 vs 31 words etc ...) given my disdain for hard arbitrary static numeric limits". Read 12:55 CST: decision plain-prose-lint keeps STE001, a CI error on a sentence over 30 words (max_words 30). The name survives in lint/ste_lint.py, actions/ste-lint, the STE0nn codes and rule anchor output-write-in-ste, against his 2026-11-02 13:22 CST ruling "drop Simplified Technical English (STE) as a named standard, everywhere". 73 of 3561 commits on main since Nov 4 fix the lint. Owner 12:56 CST: "A -- and im sure this 30 word thing is only one of many stale digit level hooks". 1. STE001 stops failing; wordiness and repetition go to reviewers and judges, which never count. 2. The lint, its action, its codes and the rule anchor drop "STE" from their names. 3. A read-only census (started 12:57 CST) lists every fixed number that refuses or fails. Each one the owner did not rule is retired, or derived from measured runs as in 3.2. Owner 13:10 CST: "on fixed numbers A". The census (scratchpad limits-census.md) lists about 45 numbers; item 3 covers each one the owner did not rule. Two contradictions go in too: merge.py warns at 70% of a job cap where decision ci-job-caps says 80%, and bin/sim-lease refuses on load average, which decision machine-load-brake forbids. Home: decision plain-prose-lint, rewritten in place.
